question: A 15-year-old male presents to the emergency department with fever, malaise, and shortness of breath for 1 week. Further history reveals that the patient experiences swelling in his face in the morning that disappears as the day progresses. Physical exam reveals hepatosplenomegaly. A complete blood count shows WBC 84,000 cells/mL. Most of this patient's leukocytes are likely to express which of the following cell surface markers?
analysis: Based on the clinical presentation of fever, malaise, shortness of breath, swelling in the face, hepatosplenomegaly, and a very high white blood cell count, the most likely diagnosis is acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). In ALL, the leukemic cells are typically of B-cell origin. CD19 is a cell surface marker that is commonly expressed on B-cells. Therefore, in this case, most of the patient's leukocytes are likely to express CD19.
